reference.notes:
I implemented the two stubs in `packages/shared/src/index.ts`. The whole package suite passes (185/185), including both Jira suites, and so does `npm test` with its coverage gate.

- **`trimTrailingSlashes`** walks backwards from the end of the string while the character is `/` (U+002F), then cuts the string there. It uses no regex and takes linear time, the same approach as the private helper in `packages/client`. Backslashes and whitespace are kept, and empty or all-slash strings come back as `""`.
- **`jiraSiteUrlSchema`** is `z.string().trim().refine(isJiraSiteUrl, JIRA_SITE_URL_MESSAGE).transform(trimTrailingSlashes)`. The private `isJiraSiteUrl` refuses any string containing `?` or `#`, so empty queries and fragments are refused too. Otherwise it requires `URL.parse(value)?.protocol === "https:"`. The URL is parsed only to check it; the output is the trimmed input string, so host casing, ports and dot segments stay as written. There is no length cap.

The other new schemas, constants and types were already written in the interface and needed no changes. No other files were touched.

One behaviour the spec doesn't decide: the URL parser accepts forms like `https:acme.atlassian.net`, so the schema accepts that string unchanged. If you want a literal `https://` prefix required, that's a one-line check.
